context.title: Farewell to the Ephesian Elders
context.summary: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece. At Troas, young Eutychus falls from a window during a long sermon and is restored. At Miletus Paul gives an emotional farewell to the Ephesian elders.
context.background: Paul is heading to Jerusalem with a collection for poor believers there, gathered from Gentile churches (Romans 15:25-26). His Miletus speech is the only speech in Acts addressed to Christian leaders, and it sounds much like his letters.

customs.term: The first day of the week
customs.note: Believers gathered to 'break bread' on the first day of the week, here in the evening, and Paul talked until midnight. Many oil lamps lit the upper room (v. 8).
The same leaders are called elders (v. 17) and overseers (v. 28) and are told to shepherd the flock.

watchFor: Paul 'kept back nothing that was profitable' (v. 20).
'It is more blessed to give than to receive' (v. 35), a saying of Jesus not recorded in the Gospels.

people.name: Paul
people.summary: Saul was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name.

people.name: Timotheus
people.summary: Honouring God, a young disciple who was Paul’s companion in many of his journeyings. His mother, Eunice, and his grandmother, Lois, are mentioned as eminent for their piety (2 Tim. 1:5).

people.name: Aristarchus
people.summary: Best ruler, native of Thessalonica (Acts 20:4), a companion of Paul (Acts 19:29; 27:2).

people.name: Tychicus
people.summary: Chance, an Asiatic Christian, a “faithful minister in the Lord” (Eph. 6:21, 22), who, with Trophimus, accompanied Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4).

people.name: Trophimus
people.summary: A foster-child, an Ephesian who accompanied Paul during a part of his third missionary journey (Acts 20:4; 21:29). He was with Paul in Jerusalem, and the Jews, supposing that the apostle had brought him with him into the temple, raised a tumult which resulted in Paul’s imprisonment.

people.name: Sopater
people.summary: The father who saves, probably the same as Sosipater, a kinsman of Paul (Rom. 16:21), a Christian of the city of Berea who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4-6).

people.name: Gaius
people.summary: A man of Derbe who accompanied Paul into Asia on his last journey to Jerusalem

people.name: Secundus
people.summary: Second, a Christian of Thessalonica who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4).

people.name: Eutychus
people.summary: Fortunate, (Acts 20:9-12), a young man of Troas who fell through drowsiness from the open window of the third floor of the house where Paul was preaching, and was “taken up dead.”

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

places.name: Macedonia
places.summary: In New Testament times, was a Roman province lying north of Greece. It was governed by a propraetor with the title of proconsul. Paul was summoned by the vision of the “man of Macedonia” to preach the gospel there (Acts 16:9).

places.name: Greece
places.summary: Orginally consisted of the four provinces of Macedonia, Epirus, Achaia, and Peleponnesus. In Acts 20:2 it designates only the Roman province of Macedonia.

places.name: Syria
places.summary: (Heb. Aram), the name in the Old Testament given to the whole country which lay to the north-east of Phoenicia, extending to beyond the Euphrates and the Tigris.

places.name: Derbe
places.summary: A small town on the eastern part of the upland plain of Lycaonia, about 20 miles from Lystra. Paul passed through Derbe on his route from Cilicia to Iconium, on his second missionary journey (Acts 16:1), and probably also on his third journey (18:23; 19:1).

places.name: Troas
places.summary: A city on the coast of Mysia, in the north-west of Asia Minor, named after ancient Troy, which was at some little distance from it (about 4 miles) to the north.

places.name: Philippi
places.summary: Formerly Crenides, “the fountain,” the capital of the province of Macedonia. It stood near the head of the Sea, about 8 miles north-west of Kavalla.

places.name: Assos
places.summary: A sea-port town of Proconsular Asia, in the district of Mysia, on the north shore of the Gulf of Adramyttium. Paul came hither on foot along the Roman road from Troas (Acts 20:13, 14), a distance of 20 miles.

places.name: Mitylene
places.summary: The chief city of the island of Lesbos, on its east coast, in the AEgean Sea. Paul, during his third missionary journey, touched at this place on his way from Corinth to Judea (Acts 20:14), and here tarried for a night.

places.name: Chios
places.summary: Mentioned in Acts 20:15, an island in the Aegean Sea, about 5 miles distant from the mainland, having a roadstead, in the shelter of which Paul and his companions anchored for a night when on his third missionary return journey.

places.name: Miletus
places.summary: (Miletum, 2 Tim. 4:20), a seaport town and the ancient capital of Ionia, about 36 miles south of Ephesus. On his voyage from Greece to Syria, Paul touched at this port, and delivered that noble and pathetic address to the elders (“presbyters,” ver. 28) of Ephesus recorded in Acts 20:15-35.

places.name: Samos
places.summary: An island in the AEgean Sea, which Paul passed on his voyage from Assos to Miletus (Acts 20:15), on his third missionary journey.

places.name: Trogyllium
places.summary: A town on the western coast of Asia Minor, where Paul “tarried” when on his way from Assos to Miletus, on his third missionary journey (Acts 20:15).

places.name: Asia
places.summary: Is used to denote Proconsular Asia, a Roman province which embraced the western parts of Asia Minor, and of which Ephesus was the capital, in Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10, 22; 20:4, 16, 18, etc., and probably Asia Minor in Acts 19:26, 27; 21:27; 24:18; 27:2.

places.name: Ephesus
places.summary: The capital of proconsular Asia, which was the western part of Asia Minor. It was colonized principally from Athens. In the time of the Romans it bore the title of “the first and greatest metropolis of Asia.”

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

events.title: Mission to Macedonia and Greece
events.summary: Passage: Acts 20:1–6. People: Trophimus, Tychicus, Timotheus, Gaius, Secundus, Aristarchus and others. Place: Philippi, Troas, Greece, Macedonia. Lasted about 1 year.

events.title: Third Missionary Journey
events.summary: Passage: Acts 18:24–20:16. People: Paul, Luke, Timotheus, Aristarchus, Aquila, Priscilla and others. Lasted about 4 years.

events.title: Eutychus revived
events.summary: Passage: Acts 20:7–12. People: Eutychus, Paul, Luke. Place: Troas.

events.title: Voyage to Miletus
events.summary: Passage: Acts 20:13–16. People: Paul, Luke. Place: Asia, Chios, Miletus, Samos. Lasted about 1 week.

events.title: Paul speaks to Ephesian Elders
events.summary: Passage: Acts 20:17–38. People: Paul, Luke. Place: Miletus. Lasted about 4 days.
